in_text_mentions: ules associated with edema and increased local temperature. Several of these lesions showed poorly defined central ulceration and eschar remnants. panels.rationale: Single H&E section from deep excisional biopsy of lower extremity lesion in case report titled Erythema Induratum of Bazin. Caption and in-text describe lobular panniculitis with fat necrosis, granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells, and medium/small-vessel vasculitis supporting Bazin's diagnosis.
panels.attribution_text: Gonzalez Quiroz et al. Erythema Induratum of Bazin Associated With a Negative Tuberculin Test: A Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.113542. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological study of subcutaneous tissue stained with hematoxylin-eosin (H&E), showing a pattern of lobular panniculitis, characterized by predominant inflammatory infiltrate in the adipose tissue lobules, with relative preservation of the interlobular septa and vasculitis (original magnifications ×100). Subcutaneous adipose tissue was observed with a predominantly lobular inflammatory infiltrate and alteration of the normal adipose architecture. The inflammatory infiltrate was composed mainly of mononuclear inflammatory cells and histiocytes, with focal areas of adipocyte degeneration and fat necrosis. Associated fibrotic and inflammatory changes were observed in the subcutaneous tissue, along with vasculitis consistent with lobular panniculitis.
in_text_mentions: n skin test (TST/PPD) was performed, which yielded a negative result with 2 mm of induration.
